text:
Maya: Heads-up — proposal for per-tenant canary flow for Dedicated customers. Idea is a "shadow+divert" phased approach: send mirrored (shadow) requests to the new model variant for 100% of requests for X hours to collect signals, then divert a small percentage (1-5%) of real traffic for N hours with circuit-breakers. Want feedback on controls and telemetry we need.

Sam: +1 on shadow first. we should avoid cold-cache overload on the dedicated pool. how do we handle KV cache separation?

Maya: good point. proposal: shadow requests run on a separate read-only cache instance that never writes back to the tenant's hot KV. divert traffic uses the normal cache so we can measure user impact.

Jonas: for diversion we need two knobs: percentage and rollout unit (by session vs by request vs by user). session-based is safer for conversational apps.

Tia: agree. also require a per-tenant concurrency cap for the canary slice so a noisy tenant can't blow the reserved pool. e.g., max_canary_qps and max_canary_concurrency settings.

Alina: telemetry checklist: p99 latency, p90/p50, error_rate (5xx + model failures), generation_cost_delta (tokens * cost), semantic_regressions metric (eval prompts), and user-visible fallback rate. + traces for request routing.

Sam: how do we express this in the API/console? Suggest a compact rollout config that admins can apply per-tenant. Something like:

```json
{
  "mode": "shadow", // shadow | divert
  "shadow_duration": "6h",
  "divert": {
    "percent": 2,
    "unit": "session",
    "max_concurrency": 50,
    "slo_guard": {"p99_ms": 1000, "error_rate_pct": 0.5}
  }
}
```

Maya: that looks good. Need to ensure console UX surfaces the safety guards and predicted cost delta up-front.

Jonas: operationally we need automatic rollback triggers: if p99 > threshold OR semantic_regressions > X OR fallback_rate > Y then revert to previous model. Should be a configurable policy.

Tia: also add a manual "force-fallback" button in console with reason required (for audit). Integrate with audit logs/KMS.

Alina: for telemetry compute baseline vs canary variant in the same time window. we should do paired comparison (per-session histogram diffs) to avoid noisy signals. add a lightweight A/B test tag so evals can correlate.

Sam: risk: tenant isolation. If divert traffic uses dedicated GPUs, spiky canary traffic could cause SLA regression for other tenants on the same pool. Suggest a quota for canary bytes/min and a QoS class for canary requests (lower priority than stable).

Maya: agreed. Implement soft throttling + emergency hard cap. Also prefer run-time placement that isolates canary instances to a small set of hosts with spare capacity.

Jonas: question re. routing: Should the routing decision live in serving runtime or controller? If runtime, it's faster for per-request session stickiness. If controller, easier to change policy.

Maya: hybrid: controller stores policy and per-tenant allocation; runtime enforces percent/unit at admission time using token buckets and sticky assignment. Controller sends a versioned policy blob to the runtime so rollout changes are atomic.

Tia: we need a lighter-weight telemetry stream for canaries — high-frequency metrics (1s/5s) for rollback triggers + aggregated hourly summaries for audit. Make sure retention is longer for canary traces (30d) to support investigations.

Alina: add a "quality-check" stage after shadowing: run daily eval set against shadow outputs and compute a regressed_prompt_count. If that crosses threshold, block divert stage.

Sam: UX: show an estimated monthly cost delta and expected token delta for the chosen percent/units in the console. otherwise customers freak out.

Maya: final ask: engineering owners — can eng-runtime implement sticky session sampling + token-bucket enforcement? can eng-platform add a per-tenant rollout API and console surfaces for the knobs above? I can PR a policy schema.

DeployBot: deploy-request queued: eng-runtime/feature/tenant-canary-sampling (owner: Jonas)

Jonas: I can own the runtime piece. will prototype sampling and sticky assignment this week. need a spec for the policy blob fields.

Maya: I'll draft a concise policy schema and a console mock, then share. thanks all — want this in Beta for two pilot Dedicated customers next month. :rocket:

Tia: adding a quick checklist for rollout readiness: 1) shadow run 24h, 2) automated daily evals pass, 3) diversion cap <= 2% for first 48h, 4) telemetry retention ok, 5) rollback policy set.

Alina: noted. I'll wire up the eval alerts.

Sam: cool. ping me when the schema PR is ready and I'll add console copy and cost calc.

Maya: done for now — will post the draft schema in #eng-platform in ~2h.
